definition: End-to-End AI Flows is a core concept in AI-Integrated Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What End-to-End AI Flows is
theory.body: End-to-End AI Flows describes the methods and patterns used within AI-Integrated Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: End-to-End AI Flows is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why End-to-End AI Flows matters
theory.body: Without End-to-End AI Flows, systems built with AI-Integrated Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How End-to-End AI Flows works
theory.body: The mechanism behind End-to-End AI Flows follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of End-to-End AI Flows.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of End-to-End AI Flows
theory.body: End-to-End AI Flows offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
